# Independent correctness review: Terra Max GEDCOM C++

- Run UID: `32c731e9-f3b1-4174-b887-8261e5269f57`.
- Raw root: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/gedcom-cpp-gpt-5.6-terra-max/gedcom-cpp/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-terra_max/eval1/run1` (called **R** below).
- Result: **169/212 passed (79.716981%); 43 failed**, no skipped tests or test errors. Build succeeded; agent and grading completed. Eval 4.0.3, Codex CLI 0.153.4, suite version 8807848.
- Recommendation: **qualifies as a naturally completed implementation result**, subject to the collection owner's ordinary provenance/publication gates. The failures are implementation omissions against the frozen public contract, not an infrastructure failure requiring regeneration.

## Correctness findings

All 43 failures accept invalid input instead of returning the required error. The implementation is substantial and implements all four CLI actions, JSON handling, GEDCOM parsing/rendering, and standard-library ZIP/DEFLATE support. Its main weakness is an incomplete semantic validator, not a missing implementation or output-envelope mismatch.

| Independent defect group | Failed tests | Evidence |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Incomplete datatype validation | 20 | `Evals/GEDCOM/tests/test_data_types.py`: invalid DATE month and non-Gregorian BCE usage (2), non-exact CHAN.DATE (1), TIME range violations (3), legacy AGE `INFANT` (1), LANG `en_US` (1), invalid FILE paths and malformed FORM media type (5), invalid latitude/longitude directions or bounds (3), invalid RESN/PEDI/NAME.TYPE/ASSO.ROLE values (4). |
| Missing context-sensitive structural requirements | 13 | `test_validation.py`: payload on HEAD.PLAC (422); missing FILE.FORM (476 and render 762); FILE.TRAN.FORM (486); ASSO.ROLE (516); MAP.LATI/LONG (528, 547); NAME.TRAN.LANG (566 and render 749); INDI.EVEN.TYPE (585); INDI.FACT.TYPE (634); PLAC.TRAN.LANG (644); top-level OBJE.TITL (render 780). |
| Missing reciprocal family links | 6 | `test_validation.py:859` parametrizes HUSB/WIFE without FAMS and CHIL without FAMC across inspect/render; assertion at 899. Pointer existence and target type are checked, but reciprocal links are not. |
| GEDZIP payload/archive consistency omitted | 4 | `test_gedzip.py`: missing FILE attachment on inspect (90), forbidden local `file:` URL (115), missing attachment on render (193), reserved `gedcom.ged` FILE reference (223). Archive-member path validation does not substitute for validating GEDCOM FILE values against archive entries. |

Source references are to `R/source/main.cpp`:

- `DatasetValidator::validate`, lines 1675–1695, validates document shape, visits nodes, and checks pointer existence/type, but never verifies family backlinks.
- The allowed-child table (1388–1450) is largely tag-based; its OBJE entry (1395) admits TITL without distinguishing record context. FILE/FORM/TRAN entries (1414–1419) list allowed children without implementing required child cardinalities.
- `has_no_payload_in_this_context` (1883–1891) omits HEAD.PLAC.
- `is_date_atom` (1908–1922) treats any syntactically valid tag as a month and strips BCE without the necessary calendar restrictions. `is_date_value` (1924–1956) does not enforce DateExact for CHAN.DATE.
- `visit` (1958–2037) checks allowed child membership (1996–2005), some payload/integer requirements (2006–2012), SEX enumeration (2013–2016), and generic DATE/SDATE (2018–2021). It lacks the remaining tested datatype and mandatory-child validation above. HEAD/GEDC/VERS special cases in `validate_document_shape` (1745–1815) do not cover these other structures.
- `inspect_gedzip` (2181–2207) extracts entries, requires `gedcom.ged`, and invokes generic GEDCOM validation, without reconciling FILE references with archive contents. `render_gedzip` (2210–2231) adds supplied attachments but similarly omits required linkage; rejecting an attachment key named `gedcom.ged` does not reject that name in a FILE payload.

The failing requirements are explicit in the frozen public `Evals/GEDCOM/prompt/docs/FamilySearchGEDCOMv7.html`: datatype sections `#date`, `#time`, `#age`, `#language`, `#file-path`, `#latitude`, and `#longitude`; structure sections `#HEADER`, `#MULTIMEDIA_RECORD`, `#ASSOCIATION_STRUCTURE`, `#PLACE_STRUCTURE`, `#PERSONAL_NAME_STRUCTURE`, `#INDIVIDUAL_EVENT_STRUCTURE`, `#INDIVIDUAL_ATTRIBUTE_STRUCTURE`, and `#CHANGE_DATE`; reciprocal linkage in `#FAMILY_RECORD`; and archive rules in `#gedzip`. The public base/technical prompts require rejecting malformed datasets. No unsupported hidden-fixture requirement was identified in these failures.
